subject: Post-call: real-time API performance priorities and trial acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Alex Hudson <alex.hudson@vectrahealth.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Today’s discovery — notes and clarifications

Monica / Ben,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick summary from our side so we’re aligned before you send a formal recap:

- Pain: Our current real-time recommendation API is spiking CPU on short bursts and tail latency is killing UX during peak windows (even though average latency looks fine).
- Current stack: Java-based microservice, gRPC frontend, in-house LRU cache, serving 2k qps peak with 300 concurrent users. Models are served on a mix of managed GPUs via a partner.
- Immediate goals: Reduce p95 across interactive flows to <350ms end-to-end for 128-token responses and ensure warm-start cold-start behavior for burst traffic.
- Constraints: Data residency stays in us-west. We can only change inference layer, not upstream business logic. Security: SOC2 compliance is required for trial.

Also attaching the sample workload we discussed (vectra-sample-workload.csv) and rough traffic heatmap. Would appreciate a short post-call doc that lays out what Redwood would propose for a 2-week trial.

Alex
Sr. Engineering Manager
Vectra Health

---
Attachment: vectra-sample-workload.csv (attachment stub)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hudson <alex.hudson@vectrahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Today’s discovery — notes and clarifications

Alex — thanks for the clear summary. Below is a concise post-call recap and the proposed acceptance criteria for the trial so your team can review with stakeholders. I’ve attached a short MOP (redwood_trial_mop.pdf) that outlines infra steps and roles.

Recap of pain points (from call):
- Tail latency spikes on interactive flows (p95 unpredictable during bursts).
- Throughput constraints during concurrent sessions (our qps per model varies widely by endpoint).
- Streaming UX degrades when tokens emit slowly; perceived latency is more important than average token time.

What Redwood heard as success for a 2-week pilot:
1) p95 end-to-end (client -> inference -> response) for 128-token prompts consistently <350ms during normal load and <500ms for short burst windows (defined as sustained 10s windows at 1.5x baseline).
2) Support for streaming responses for the primary endpoint with startup token emission <80ms and smooth subsequent token pacing.
3) Stable concurrency: handle 300 concurrent active sessions with acceptable queuing (<50ms median queue time).
4) No production data leaves us-west, SOC2 evidence provided, and audit logs accessible for the trial.

Technical notes and proposed approach:
- We recommend a canary using Redwood Dedicated with a small reserved pool (N GPUs) + autoscale buffer. We’ll enable prefix KV caching for warm conversation reuse and set batching thresholds tuned to your 128-token median.
- For streaming UX: enable continuous flushing with smaller micro-batches so the first token is emitted quickly; we’ll instrument token emission traces so you can see perceived latency per session.
- For tails: we’ll run a short kernel selection pass and a quantization test on a shadow copy of your model (no changes to upstream code required).

Acceptance checklist for trial (what we’ll measure together):
- p95 token emission and end-to-end p95 under baseline and burst profiles (you provided the CSV).
- Concurrency profile and queue time heatmap.
- Cost estimate per 1M tokens for the observed workload (post-trial).
- SOC2 artifact package and audit log access validation.

Next steps / owners:
- Monica: send MOP + trial onboarding link and HubSpot deal (today) — action: share trial timeline and required infra creds.
- Ben: connect with procurement for the contract addendum and trial SOW (EOD Fri).
- Karthik (SE): run a short kernel-selection test on a model snapshot and report initial perf numbers by Mon.
- Alex / Priya: confirm SOC2 point-of-contact and whether we need a CNDA.

Proposed calendar:
- Trial kickoff (canary): Mon, Apr 26 — quick 30-min kickoff to provision resources and validate creds.
- Checkpoint 1: Wed, Apr 28 — initial perf readout.
- Final review: Fri, May 7 — consolidated metrics and next-step recommendation.

Attachments: redwood_trial_mop.pdf (MOP with roles & infra commands), vectra-sample-workload.csv (your upload)

If that reads correctly I’ll create the HubSpot activity and send the onboarding link.

Thanks — looking forward.

Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
